title: Curriculum coverage map ("Ofsted view")
description: A coloured grid: rows = pupils, columns = NC / GCSE spec points (AQA / Edexcel / OCR / CIE / SQA / CCEA / White Rose). Cell colour = mastery from worksheet results. Click an empty cell → generates a targeted worksheet. Click a red cell → re-teach. Turns generated worksheets into evidenced curriculum coverage and is the single biggest reason a Head of Department buys site-wide.
rationale: User's improvement #3. PC10 (PR #35) already produces per-question coverage data inside `metadata.coverageMap`. PB1 (Phase B · PR-1) per-question provenance fills the rest. This PR builds the cross-pupil aggregation layer + the interactive grid UI.
steps: Audit data sources: each worksheet's metadata.coverageMap + metadata.questionProvenance (PB1) + assignment submissions + scan-mark per-question correctness. Confirm pupil_id × spec_ref × mastery is reconstructable.
Create client/src/lib/coverageAggregator.ts:
- aggregateCoverage(pupils, worksheets, scanResults, opts: { board: 'aqa'|'edexcel'|'ocr'|'cie'|'sqa'|'ccea'|'white-rose'|'all'; subject; yearGroup }): CoverageMatrix

Returns: { rows: pupilId[]; cols: { specRef; specTitle; ao; bloomLevel }[]; cells: Record<pupilId, Record<specRef, { status: 'unseen'|'green'|'amber'|'red'; lastSeenAt: string; evidence: { worksheetId; questionIdx; markPct }[] }>> }.
- Mastery rules: green ≥80% across last 3 attempts, amber 50–79%, red <50%, unseen = no question on that spec ever served to the pupil.
Create client/src/lib/specPointTaxonomy.ts:
- Static taxonomy generators per board: getSpecPointsAQA(subject, yearGroup) → { specRef; specTitle; ao; tier?; band? }[].

- Bundled JSON files committed under client/src/data/spec-points/ — one per (board, subject, yearGroup). Bootstrap with AQA Maths, AQA English Language, AQA Combined Science (Y10–11) since Pillar A already has anchor data for those.
- Add a small CLI script tools/import-spec-points.ts that ingests a CSV of spec points (DfE / awarding-body PDF tables converted) into the JSON files; document the input format.
Create client/src/pages/CurriculumCoverage.tsx (new route /coverage):
- Filter bar: board (AQA default), subject, year group, class.
- Renders the coverage matrix as a sticky-header / sticky-first-column grid. Cells colour-coded; tooltip shows last-seen date + evidence count.
- Click an unseen cell → opens the worksheet Auto-from-class panel (Phase A) pre-filled with that pupil + that spec ref → Generate.
- Click a red cell → opens a re-teach worksheet generator (Phase B PB3) pre-filled with the pupil + the misconception ids associated with that spec.
- 'Export coverage CSV' button — useful for evidence packs / Ofsted deep dives.
- Performance: virtualise the grid with @tanstack/react-virtual for ≥ 200 pupils × ≥ 80 specs.
Wire navigation: add /coverage to App.tsx and the Settings → Tools list. Hide behind feature flag `COVERAGE_MAP_ENABLED` while spec-point taxonomy is bootstrapping.
Tests:
- client/src/lib/__tests__/coverageAggregator.test.ts — coverage rules, last-3 window, unseen vs green vs red, multi-board filtering.
- Snapshot of CurriculumCoverage.tsx with a 5-pupil × 10-spec fixture.
do_not_touch: Worksheet generation pipeline — coverage is read-only consumer of metadata
PB3 re-teach planner — PC4 only routes into it
acceptance_criteria: /coverage renders for an AQA Maths Y10 class with at least 30 pupils and 60 spec points without lag.
Clicking an unseen cell opens Auto-from-class with the right pupil + spec pre-fill.
Clicking a red cell opens a PB3 re-teach for that misconception.
Export CSV produces one row per (pupil, spec) with status + last-seen + evidence count.
coverageAggregator.test.ts passes with the documented mastery thresholds.
pnpm run check + pnpm run build + pnpm test --run pass.
verification: Manual: /coverage on a real-looking dataset; click each cell colour at least once.

size_estimate.notes: above 600 — bundle the spec-point JSONs as a separate sibling PR if a fresh chat needs to

context_budget_for_fresh_chat: MEDIUM. coverageMapBuilder.ts (PC10) + class-auto-brief.ts are the only existing files needing a read.
